predecessors.name: Wattasid dynasty
predecessors.text: Fez and the Wattasid north, taken on 28 January 1549 and finally in September 1554

predecessors.name: Songhai Empire
predecessors.text: the Niger bend from Timbuktu to Gao and Djenné, taken from 1591

successors.name: Dila'iya Sultanate
successors.text: Fez, Meknes and the north, held by the Dila'iya from 1641 to 1668

successors.name: Pashalik of Timbuktu
successors.text: the Niger bend, a Moroccan governorate 1591-1621, then Arma-ruled

successors.name: Bou Regreg Republic
successors.text: Salé, the 'Republic of Salé' on the Bou Regreg

ledger.x: 1510: the Saadi sultanate is established at Tidsi.
1513: the Saadi seat moves from Tidsi to Afughal (infobox 'Afughal (1513-1525)').
1524: Ahmad al-Araj takes Marrakesh.
1525: Marrakesh becomes the Saadi capital (infobox 'Marrakesh (1525-1659)').
1541: Muhammad al-Shaykh takes Agadir.
1541: the Portuguese leave Safi and Azemmour.
28 January 1549: the Saadians take Fez.
1550: the Portuguese evacuate Ksar es-Seghir and Asilah.
June 1550: the Saadians take Tlemcen.
February 1551: Ottoman forces drive the Saadians out of Tlemcen.
January 1554: the Ottoman-backed Abu Hassun defeats the Saadians and holds Fez.
September 1554: Muhammad al-Shaykh retakes Fez; the Wattasid dynasty is finished.
1556: Muhammad al-Shaykh occupies Taghaza.
1557: the first Saadi occupation of Taghaza ends.
1583: Ahmad al-Mansur's forces occupy the Touat and Gourara oases.
1586: Saadi forces occupy the Taghaza salt mines again.
1589: Asilah goes to Spain.
March 1591: the Moroccans defeat the Songhai at Tondibi.
30 May 1591: Timbuktu falls and the Niger bend becomes a Moroccan governorate.
1591: the Pashalik of Timbuktu is founded.
1592: Djenné falls to the Moroccans.
1603: Ahmad al-Mansur dies of the plague (25 August) and the realm splits for 25 years between a region ruled from Marrakesh and one ruled from Fez (infobox 'Fez (1603-1627, rival capital)').
1610: the Fez line cedes Larache to Spain.
1614: the Souss leaves Saadi control for the Zawiya of Illigh.
August 1614: Spain takes La Mamora (Mehdya) on the Sebou estuary.
1618: direct control of the Sudan ends.
1627: the two Saadian splinter states 'in Marrakesh and Fes were finally reunified' and Marrakesh is again the only capital.
1631: Abu Hassun of Iligh takes the Draa valley.
1631: the Tafilalt leaves the Saadi realm; Mawlay al-Sharif is 'declared sultan of the Tafilalt in 1631' and the morocco dossier founds the Alawi state at Sijilmasa in the same year.
1641: the Dila'iya take Fez, Meknes and Salé.
1641: the rest of the Dila'iya domain leaves the Saadi realm.

1641: the rest of the realm outside Marrakesh leaves Saadi control and no page names a holder: Tadla-Azilal, Doukkala-Abda, the Oriental (the east), the remainder of the Middle Atlas and the Tafilalt region, and the southern edge (about 150,000 km2).
1659: the Saadi dynasty ends.

wars.name: Saadi conquest of the Wattasid realm
wars.outcome: The Saadians took Marrakesh in 1524 (or 1525), partitioned Morocco 'roughly along the Oum Er-Rbia River' by the 1527 Treaty of Tadla, took Fez on 28 January 1549 and, after the Ottoman-backed Abu Hassun's January 1554 victory, retook it in September 1554.

wars.name: Saadi-Ottoman struggle over Tlemcen
wars.outcome: The Saadians conquered Tlemcen in June 1550; Ottoman forces expelled them in February 1551.

wars.name: Battle of the Three Kings (Wadi al-Makhazin)
wars.outcome: The armies met 'at Wadi al-Makhazin near Ksar al-Kebir on August 4' and the Saadians won; Abd al-Malik I died in the battle and Ahmad al-Mansur succeeded.

wars.name: Moroccan invasion of the Songhai Empire
wars.outcome: Judar Pasha left Marrakesh in October 1590, reached the Niger on 28 February 1591 and won at Tondibi on 13 March 1591; Gao and Timbuktu (30 May) fell in 1591 and Djenné in 1592.

wars.name: Saadi succession war (Marrakesh and Fez lines)
wars.outcome: After al-Mansur's death 'the Saadian realm was split between a region ruled from Marrakesh and a region ruled from Fes' for 25 years; reunified in 1627.

wars.name: Dila'iya-Saadi war
wars.outcome: The Dila'iya defeated a Saadian army in 1638 (Saadi page) and by 1641 had taken Meknes, Fez and Salé, expelling the Saadi family from Fez.

certainty.note: No treaty line is on the pages except the roughly drawn Oum Er-Rbia partition of 1527; the Saharan and Niger holdings, the Touat and Taghaza, and the 1641-1659 rump around Marrakesh are approximate.
